name: the server says what it is
why: zou answers /health with its own version rather than claiming to be a GoTrue release it is not. The name and the description are upstream's, so a client checking what it is talking to still reads GoTrue.

name: what a sign in screen reads before it draws itself
why: saml_private_key_next_configured. Upstream answers true with SAML off and no key of any kind configured, which reads as an inverted flag, and zou answers false. Nothing in the clients reads it while saml_enabled is false.

name: listing accounts
why: zou fills the identity list in and upstream answers identities null here, because its ORM does not load the association on the listing query. Factors are the same story on the same query: zou lists them and upstream leaves the key out. A client reading either off a listed account gets it from zou and has to fetch each account again from upstream, and nothing can be branching on a null that the single account fetch never returns.

name: listing accounts a page at a time
why: Asking for a page does not change which columns the listing loads, so this is the identities and factors difference above on a page of one. The link and the total the case is here for both match.

name: the last page of a listing
why: The identities and factors difference above, on the page after the first. The link the case is here for, which names a previous page and no next one, matches.

name: the total when a filter narrows the listing
why: The identities and factors difference above, with a filter in front of it. The count the case is here for, which is the filtered rows and not all of them, matches.

name: a method nobody supports
why: zou answers 400 validation_failed and upstream answers 500. Upstream's check on a challenge never looks at the method at all, so a method it does not know gets through validation and falls over later, inside the code that writes the flow state, where the failure is reported as an internal one. There are only two methods and a client that sent a third made a mistake it can be told about, so zou tells it. Nothing that sends s256 or plain sees a difference, and a 400 is the answer a 500 was standing in for.

name: the signing keys, which there are none of while the secret is symmetric
why: zou publishes one EC key here and upstream publishes an empty set. A project on zou derives a P-256 key from its own jwt secret and signs its access tokens with it, the way a project created on Supabase today does, because a library that verifies a caller for itself reads this endpoint and matches on the key id in the token header. Upstream answers an empty set because a GoTrue configured with a symmetric secret and no signing keys file has nothing to publish, which is a local dev arrangement rather than what a hosted project looks like. Nothing that verifies against the secret is affected: tokens signed under the legacy format keep verifying against it.
